title: Handshake blueprint: SDK ergonomics + tool-schema PRD (draft)
body:
Overview:
This document outlines a proposal for a lightweight handshake and schema-first tool-call contract intended to improve hosted-api streaming ergonomics for client SDKs. The goal is a minimal, predictable client surface that supports: incremental partial responses, typed tool invocation (with idempotent resumes), and low-footprint mobile/edge SDKs. This is a product PRD draft — design + rollout plan + open questions.

Problem statement:
- Developers building streaming experiences need a clear contract for when the model will emit partial text, when it will request a tool, and how the client should surface progress and retries.
- Current ad-hoc tool-call frames lead to inconsistent SDK behavior, fragile resume semantics, and poor telemetry correlation across truncated sessions.
- Mobile/IoT clients require a small binary and a synchronous-friendly API while web/desktop clients prefer evented streaming.

Design principles:
1) Minimal on-ramp: default behavior should "just work" for basic streaming text without extra config.
2) Schema-first tool calls: each tool invocation is declared with a concise JSON schema (name, version, args-schema) before execution.
3) Atomic tool frames: tool-call begin / tool-output / tool-end frames are idempotent and referenceable by an invocation-id.
4) Resumeable partials: partial-response checkpoints include a compact KV prefix token (opaque) that the runtime can use to resume from the same logical output position.
5) Backwards compatible: older clients must gracefully ignore unknown frames while preserving core streaming text.

Protocol sketch (high level):
- Stream frames are newline-delimited JSON with an envelope.type field: text_chunk | tool_begin | tool_event | tool_result | checkpoint | heartbeat | end.
- tool_begin: {invocation_id, tool_name, schema_id, hints} emitted by model when it decides to call a tool. SDK may choose to auto-fulfill or surface a callback.
- tool_event: streaming progress from the tool (optional).
- tool_result: final structured output (typed) with provenance metadata and optional human-facing text.
- checkpoint: lightweight resume token + last_commit_offset; produced periodically and on tool boundaries.

API ergonomics (SDK surface):
- Two client bindings: Evented (on('chunk'), on('tool'), on('checkpoint')) and Blocking (await stream.nextPartial()).
- Default client constructor opts: {resume: true, schemaValidation: "warn", prefetchTools: "auto|none|manual"}.
- Tool handlers: registerTool(name, handlerFn | remoteProxy) -> returns small descriptor. Handler receives typed args that have been validated by default.
- Fallbacks: if SDK receives unknown tool_begin and no handler is registered, sdk emits a tool-suggested-fallback event for the app to decide.

Structured output and schema versioning:
- Schemas are named (tool:contacts.lookup v1) and referenced by schema_id; runtime stores forward-compatible diffs.
- SDKs should support a validation mode: strict (reject tool_result mismatches), warn (emit telemetry but pass through), lax (always pass). Default is warn.
- For iterative UX (autocomplete, partial tables), tool_result can include partial=true until final. Each partial result is idempotent when tagged with sequence numbers.

Telemetry and observability:
- Required signals: partial_latency_p50/p95, tool_invoke_rate, tool_resolve_latency, resume_success_rate, unknown_tool_rate, schema_validation_failures.
- Each frame includes a small metadata header with correlation_id (traceable to request id) and token_count delta.
- Console dashboard: per-model stream fidelity, tool-resolve distribution, and resume delta trendline (tokens saved by checkpointing).

Performance targets and safety tradeoffs:
- Streaming latency target: p50 < 60ms chunk emission for short replies (<=64 tokens); p95 < 250ms.
- Tool-call roundtrip SLA: best-effort for hosted toollets; recommended integrations should surface median <200ms.
- Checkpointing cadence tuned to latency vs cost: default every 128 tokens or on tool boundaries.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha (4 weeks): server-side emit of handshake frames + experimental JS SDK evented binding in devhub for internal teams.
2) Beta opt-in (8–10 weeks): enable schema-first tool calls for customers via feature flag; publish migration guide.
3) GA (12–16 weeks): SDKs (js, python, java), telemetry dashboards, and migration tooling for existing sessions.

Migration guidance for existing clients:
- Default behavior is noop: legacy clients continue to get plain text chunks. New SDKs will parse and forward legacy chunks.
- Provide a shim: small JS runtime that transforms older token-streams into new envelope frames for environments where server migration is partial.

Security and privacy notes:
- Tool arguments may contain PII; tool handlers must declare data retention policies in schema metadata.
- Handshake frames include only schema ids and hashes for tool discovery; full schemas retrieved via an authenticated manifest URL when needed.

Open questions:
- Should the server generate ephemeral tool credentials for remote handler invocation or leave auth to the app? Pros/cons documented but need security team signoff.
- Checkpoint token format: opaque blob (easy) vs compressed deterministic prefix (better dedupe). Tradeoff: portability vs server complexity.
- Mobile offline semantics: queue tool calls locally vs surface deferred action. Which is primary for our mobile SDK?

Next steps and owners:
- Prototype: SDK evented binding + server frame emitter (Eng: Diego Morales, 3w).
- Telemetry schema: product + observability (Lena Fischer, 2w).
- Security review: data-in-tool arguments (Samira Patel, 1w).
- Draft migration guide and example app (Avery Chen, 2w).

Appendix (examples):
- Example tool_begin frame: {"type":"tool_begin", "invocation_id":"inv-2ab3", "tool_name":"calendar.create", "schema_id":"calendar.create:v1", "hints":{"timezone":"UTC"}}
- Example tool_result frame: {"type":"tool_result", "invocation_id":"inv-2ab3", "result":{"event_id":"evt-29", "start":"2026-03-12T15:00:00Z"}, "provenance":{"handler":"internal-calendar-service"}, "sequence":0, "partial":false}

This draft intentionally favors pragmatism: small, composable frames, clear SDK defaults, and an incremental rollout that keeps legacy clients functional. Feedback welcome — especially from SDK leads and mobile engineering on the blocking/async bindings tradeoffs.
